section: Discipline and Training Children (Proverbs of Solomon)

heading.en: The direction that lasts a lifetime

body.en:
'Whoever spares the rod hates their children, but the one who loves their children is careful to discipline them.' Proverbs links discipline directly to love — genuine love includes caring enough to correct, not just to please.

'Whoever disregards discipline despises themselves, but whoever heeds correction gains understanding.' Refusing correction, the book says, isn't strength — it's actually a kind of self-harm.

'Discipline your children while there is hope, and do not be a willing party to their death.' Strong language, showing just how seriously Proverbs takes the long-term stakes of how a child is raised.

One of the most famous parenting verses in the entire Bible: 'start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.' Early direction, the book promises, shapes the whole trajectory of a life.

'Discipline your children, and they will give you peace; neglect them, and they will bring you shame.' Loving correction, given consistently and early, is presented as one of the greatest gifts a parent can offer.

verse.en: Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it.

label.en: Activity sheet: Train Up a Child

body.en:
Big idea: Proverbs treats discipline as an essential expression of parental love, not its opposite — the absence of correction is described as a form of neglect or even hatred, while consistent, loving discipline is framed as one of a parent's most important responsibilities, with lasting, lifelong impact ("even when old, they will not turn from it"). This theme speaks directly to parents reading these guides as much as to children hearing the lessons.

Conversation starters: (1) Why might Proverbs connect discipline so directly to love, rather than seeing them as opposites? (2) What does "start children off on the way they should go" suggest about the importance of early years? (3) For parents: how does this shape how you think about discipline in your own home?

Pray for wisdom in how discipline and correction are given and received in your family, recognizing it as an expression of genuine love.
